cards.name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index / v5.0.1
cards.question: How do configurations compare on AA’s current intelligence index?
cards.tests: An index combining nine evaluations in four weighted groups.
cards.matters: A broad, independently reported selection of model capabilities.
cards.read: AA regraded CritPt v2 in November 2026. Version 5.0.1 scores cannot be compared directly with older index versions; differences do not establish a capability regression. This is a 27-configuration server-rendered selection, not the complete leaderboard. Model release dates are not evaluation dates.

variants.label: v5.0.1 / 27 available configurations
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: WebDev Arena / Frontend / November 13
cards.question: Which frontend outputs do people prefer?
cards.tests: Human votes compare web development outputs.
cards.matters: Preference is one perspective on generated interfaces.
cards.read: First 20 of 158 configurations from the November 13 snapshot, with 872,612 votes overall. Published bounds have unspecified confidence coverage. Preference is not screenshot fidelity or functional completion; token prices are not task costs.

variants.label: Frontend / November 13 / first 20 of 158
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: DesignArena / Website / November 16
cards.question: Which website designs do people prefer?
cards.tests: Visitors compare generated websites in pairwise votes.
cards.matters: Design preference measures a different outcome from task completion.
cards.read: First 15 visible Website HTML non-agentic rows of 187 at 14:07 UTC. The page labels MoE as a percentage while its footer and methodology describe uncertainty differently; the original label is retained without plotting it as an Elo interval. Reported time aggregation is unspecified.

variants.label: Website / November 16 / first 15 of 187
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: BioBasicsBench / xhigh
cards.question: How well do AI agents handle routine wet-lab science questions?
cards.tests: 100 tasks, five attempts per model setting, scored for rubric credit.
cards.matters: The tasks examine scientific reasoning relevant to routine laboratory work.
cards.read: Scores are mean reward, not task completion. The seven xhigh settings are the author’s comparable table; a figure includes other settings. Confidence intervals are 95% task-cluster bootstrap intervals. Output tokens are not measured task costs. Evaluation dates were not disclosed.

variants.label: OpenAI report / seven xhigh settings
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: HealthBench Professional / AA length-adjusted
cards.question: How do reported Fable settings score on clinician conversations?
cards.tests: 525 clinician conversations, four repeats and physician-written rubrics.
cards.matters: This tests responses on simulated professional medical conversations.
cards.read: These are AA independently evaluated length-adjusted scores using GPT-5.4 low as judge, not the raw score or the separate OpenAI deployment cohort. This selection contains the three configurations explicitly reported in the source summary. Run dates and task costs for these rows are not disclosed.

variants.label: AA / three reported Fable settings
limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.

cards.name: RoboDojo-RC / Tier 1 / November 16
cards.question: How much progress do robot systems make on selected real-world tasks?
cards.tests: The author evaluates six adapted physical tasks with 120 attempts per configuration; human rubrics allow partial progress.
cards.matters: These are real robot trials under a specific task selection and controller setup.
cards.read: The values are average partial-progress scores, not task completion rates. Authors selected the six easiest tasks after evaluating Astra on 18 tasks; that selection limits generalization. LLMs and vision-language-action models use different control limits, cost bases and time definitions. Estimated costs and reported times are kept in each source record; the plot compares score only. Model release dates do not establish evaluation dates. This is separate from the older RoboDojo-RealEval cohort. Carbon was evaluated in early access. Robocurve lists its release as November 10, while Google and AA list October 28; the conflicting source date is retained without assigning a normalized release date.

variants.label: RoboDojo-RC Tier 1 / 14 configurations

settings.selection: Six easiest tasks selected after Astra was evaluated on 18.

limitations: Exact evaluation dates are not reported.
